choice_context: Consumers choosing between wine options based on flavor, structure, and experience.
reasoning: The 15 most important unipolar features were selected based on their ability to subsume multiple themes, their distinctiveness, and their relevance to individual variation in wine preferences. Each feature represents a single quality that can be present in varying degrees and is not a forced contrast between two opposing qualities.

dimensions.name: Fruit Intensity

low_pole.label: Low fruit
low_pole.description: Minimal or no detectable fruit character; more neutral or earthy.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers savory or mineral-driven wines.

high_pole.label: High fruit
high_pole.description: Prominent, ripe, and forward fruit flavors and aromas.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys bold, fruit-forward reds or tropical/citrus whites.

example_contrast.high_option: Zinfandel or Syrah from warm climate

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the prominence and ripeness of fruit character in aroma and flavor.

dimensions.name: Body and Structure

low_pole.label: Light-bodied
low_pole.description: Delicate, low tannin, low alcohol, and low intensity on the palate.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers easy-drinking, sessionable wines.

high_pole.label: Full-bodied
high_pole.description: Rich, weighty, and intense on the palate with high tannin or alcohol.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys structured, bold reds or rich whites.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on perceived weight, intensity, and tannin/alcohol presence on the palate.

dimensions.name: Acidity

low_pole.label: Low acidity
low_pole.description: Smooth, flat, or flabby mouthfeel with little zing or freshness.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers softer, rounder wines.

high_pole.label: High acidity
high_pole.description: Bright, crisp, and refreshing with a lively mouthfeel.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys unoaked whites or high-acid reds.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the perceptible sharpness, freshness, and mouthwatering quality.

dimensions.name: Oak Influence

low_pole.label: Unoaked
low_pole.description: Fresh, clean, and unadulterated by oak aging or barrel fermentation.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers crisp, natural, or modern styles.

high_pole.label: Oaked
high_pole.description: Smoky, buttery, or vanilla notes from oak aging or barrel fermentation.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys aged or complex reds or oaked whites.

example_contrast.high_option: Château Latour or Napa Cabernet Sauvignon

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the presence and intensity of oak-derived flavors and textures.

dimensions.name: Sweetness

low_pole.label: Dry
low_pole.description: No perceptible residual sugar; clean and crisp finish.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers traditional, food-friendly wines.

high_pole.label: Sweet
high_pole.description: Noticeable residual sugar with a sweet or off-dry finish.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys dessert wines or sweet whites.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the perceptible sweetness on the palate and finish.

dimensions.name: Aromatic Complexity

low_pole.label: Simple nose
low_pole.description: Limited or straightforward aromas with little nuance.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers direct, easy-to-understand wines.

high_pole.label: Complex nose
high_pole.description: Layered, evolving, and nuanced aromas with multiple dimensions.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys aged or terroir-driven wines.

example_contrast.high_option: Burgundy Grand Cru or aged Barolo

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the number and evolution of detectable aromas.

dimensions.name: Earthy/Savory Character

low_pole.label: Fruity focus
low_pole.description: Minimal earthy or savory notes; more fruit-driven and clean.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers bright, fruit-forward wines.

high_pole.label: Earthy/savory
high_pole.description: Prominent notes of soil, herbs, mushrooms, or umami-like flavors.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys rustic, food-friendly reds or aged whites.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the presence and intensity of earthy or savory notes.

dimensions.name: Aging Potential

low_pole.label: Drink now
low_pole.description: Meant to be consumed young; lacks structure or tannin for aging.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers approachable, early-drinking wines.

high_pole.label: Aging potential
high_pole.description: High tannin, acidity, or alcohol that allows for long-term cellaring.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys structured, collectible wines.

example_contrast.high_option: Barolo Riserva or Bordeaux First Growth

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the wine's structural components that support aging.

dimensions.name: Traditional Style

low_pole.label: Modern style
low_pole.description: Clean, fruit-forward, and made with modern techniques.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers accessible, contemporary wines.

high_pole.label: Traditional style
high_pole.description: Old-world, terroir-driven, and made with minimal intervention.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who values heritage and authenticity.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the wine's adherence to traditional winemaking and terroir expression.

dimensions.name: Value for Money

low_pole.label: Premium price
low_pole.description: High cost relative to perceived quality or enjoyment.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prioritizes quality over cost.

high_pole.label: Good value
high_pole.description: High quality relative to price; approachable and satisfying.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who prioritizes affordability and enjoyment.

example_contrast.high_option: Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc or Kim Crawford Chardonnay

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the perceived quality-to-price ratio.

dimensions.name: Effervescence

low_pole.label: Still wine
low_pole.description: No bubbles or carbonation; smooth and still.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers traditional reds or whites.

high_pole.label: Sparkling
high_pole.description: Perfected bubbles with a lively, effervescent mouthfeel.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys celebratory or refreshing sparkling wines.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the presence and quality of bubbles.

dimensions.name: Playfulness

low_pole.label: Serious style
low_pole.description: Formal, traditional, and conventional in presentation and branding.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who values classic, elegant wines.

high_pole.label: Playful style
high_pole.description: Unconventional, whimsical, or experimental in branding or presentation.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys novelty or quirky wines.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the wine's branding, label, or unconventional presentation.

dimensions.name: Tropical Aroma Intensity

low_pole.label: Non-tropical
low_pole.description: No detectable tropical fruit aromas; more citrus or stone fruit.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers traditional or European-style whites.

high_pole.label: Tropical
high_pole.description: Prominent aromas of pineapple, mango, or passionfruit.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys New World or warm-climate whites.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the presence and intensity of tropical fruit aromas.

dimensions.name: Sessionability

low_pole.label: High alcohol
low_pole.description: Full-bodied, high ABV, and less suited for drinking in quantity.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys bold, intense wines.

high_pole.label: Low alcohol
high_pole.description: Light-bodied, low ABV, and easy to drink in quantity.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys casual, everyday wines.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the wine's alcohol content and perceived drinkability in quantity.

dimensions.name: Floral Aroma Intensity

low_pole.label: Non-floral
low_pole.description: No detectable floral notes; more fruit or earthy character.
low_pole.typical_person: Someone who prefers bold or savory wines.

high_pole.label: Floral
high_pole.description: Prominent aromas of rose, lavender, or jasmine.
high_pole.typical_person: Someone who enjoys aromatic whites or rosés.

dimensions.scoring_guidance: Rate based on the presence and intensity of floral aromas.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Both relate to fruit character, but Fruit Intensity is broader and includes all fruit types, while Tropical Aroma Intensity is a subset focused on tropical notes.
redundancy_check.resolution: Tropical Aroma Intensity is a specific flavor profile within the broader Fruit Intensity dimension and is kept as a separate feature to capture distinct preferences.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Both relate to structure, but Body and Structure is about immediate sensory experience, while Aging Potential is about future development.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are distinct because one is about current perception and the other about potential evolution over time.

redundancy_check.correlation_note: Both relate to acidity, but Balanced Acidity and Richness is about harmony between acidity and other elements, while Acidity is about the raw intensity of acidity.
redundancy_check.resolution: They are distinct because one is about balance and the other is about a single attribute.
